transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I’ve got a cough that just won’t go away, and it’s been bothering me.
When did you first notice the cough, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
It’s only been a few days, really. It came on gradually after I’d had a cold.
Could you tell me how much the cough is affecting your day-to-day life, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It’s disturbing my sleep most nights, and I’d rate it about 6 out of 10. As for medicines, I don’t have any known drug allergies.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have taken recently, and any past health problems or operations you’ve had?

I use a blue salbutamol inhaler, now 4–5 times a day instead of my usual twice, and Fostair 100/6 two puffs twice daily, plus lisinopril 10 mg once daily for blood pressure. I’ve had COPD for 8 years, and I can’t recall any operations.
Since the cough started, have you noticed anything else going on with your body?

I’m bringing up white-to-yellow phlegm, more than my usual morning phlegm, and I get a bit more breathless than usual walking to the shop. I haven’t coughed up blood, lost weight, had night sweats, or had chest pain.
Where do you feel the cough most in your body, and does it spread anywhere?
I haven’t really noticed it being in one particular place or spreading anywhere. It’s just a cough in my chest, mainly.
Besides the inhalers and lisinopril you mentioned, are you taking any other medicines for your COPD or any other health condition, even if only now and then?
No, I’m not taking anything else for my COPD or any other condition. Just those inhalers and the lisinopril.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make your cough better or worse?
Cold air and talking for a long time set it off, and steam inhalation helps a little.
Can you describe how your cough has been over time — whether it’s there all the time or comes and goes, how often it happens, and whether you notice it more at certain times of day?
It began about three weeks ago after a cold, and it comes in fits rather than being there all the time — worst in the morning and at night, with each fit lasting a few minutes.
I want to make sure I have this right — did your cough start a few days ago and come on gradually after a cold, or did it begin about three weeks ago after a cold?
Sorry, I got that wrong earlier — it began about three weeks ago, after a cold.
Besides your COPD, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly?
Just the COPD and my blood pressure, really — I don’t see anyone regularly for anything else.
What worries you most about this cough, and what are you hoping to get from today’s visit?
I’m worried my lungs are getting worse, or that it could be cancer. I’d like to get it checked and know whether something needs doing.
Since the cough started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder, bowel habits or breathing — or is everything else about the same?
My sleep’s been disturbed most nights, and I’m a bit more breathless than usual walking to the shop; otherwise I haven’t noticed changes in appetite, weight, energy, or bladder and bowel habits.
Can you tell me what your cough feels like when it happens?
It comes in fits that last a few minutes, and I’m bringing up white-to-yellow phlegm — more than my usual morning phlegm.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed since the cough started that you haven’t mentioned yet?
No, I haven’t noticed anything else beyond what I’ve mentioned.
When the cough comes on, does it feel more like a tickle in your throat, a dryness or scratchiness, or something coming up from your chest — or are you not sure?
I’m not really sure — it mostly feels like I’m bringing phlegm up from my chest.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
